description: Phaser 3 2D game starter on Vite — arcade physics, one scene, sprite-first game loop with input + update + resize wired from first render.

buildHints.whenToUse: 2D browser games — platformers, arcade, tower defense, match-3, tile-based roguelikes. Pick this over three.js when the primary surface is a 2D canvas with sprites + physics, not 3D geometry.
firstSteps: Install: `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173. The starter shows a bouncing sprite in a single Scene.
Add new scenes under `src/scenes/` and register them in the `scene` array of the Phaser.Game config in `src/main.ts`.
Put art assets in `public/assets/` and load them with `this.load.image('key', 'assets/foo.png')` inside a Scene's `preload()`.
Arcade physics is enabled by default — enable per-body via `this.physics.add.sprite(x, y, key)`.
Build: `pnpm build` emits static assets to `dist/` — ship to any static host.
gotchas: `this` inside `preload/create/update` is the Scene, not the Game. If you extract callbacks, bind or use arrow functions — losing `this` silently breaks asset loading.
Phaser clamps `update(time, delta)` delta — you cannot assume 1/60s between frames on throttled tabs. Always scale movement by `delta / 1000`.
Sprite textures are cached by key — loading the same key twice is a no-op after the first. Use distinct keys per asset or call `this.textures.remove(key)` before reloading.
Canvas size is controlled by the Phaser.Game config `scale` property, NOT by CSS. Setting CSS width/height stretches the canvas and breaks pointer coordinates.
architectureNotes: One Phaser.Game instance per page. Scenes are the unit of composition — add, switch, pause, resume.
Keep game state in the Scene (or a Scene's Registry); do NOT attach it to window/global. Scene transitions clear local state.

placeholders.description: Default scene with a bouncing sprite + input handler. Replace the sprite + logic with the product's actual game loop; keep the scene lifecycle hooks (preload/create/update).
